case.title: Hon. Amadi Ernest Anor v. Uzo-Uwani Local Government Area
claimants: Other claimants (names not specified in judgment)

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Complaint and Statement of Facts filed on 4th November 2014.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Preliminary objection filed by Defendant on 7th April 2015 challenging jurisdiction.
interlocutory_applications: Preliminary objection dated 7th April 2015 praying for dismissal of suit for lack of jurisdiction.
procedural_events: Claimants filed Complaint and Statement of Facts on 4th November 2014.
Defendant filed preliminary objection on 7th April 2015.
Claimants filed Counter-affidavit and written address on 16th April 2015.
Defendant filed reply on points of law and further affidavit.

material_facts: Claimants were elected and served as councillors of the Defendant for two terms: 2008/2009 and 2010/2011.
They finished their second term at the end of December 2011.
They were not paid their severance allowance.
Claimants' counsel wrote a pre-action notice dated 19th August 2014.
Defendant replied by letter dated 2nd September 2014 stating it would not pay.

chronology.event: Claimants served first term as councillors.
Claimants served second term as councillors.
Claimants finished second term; severance allowance obligation arose.
Claimants' counsel wrote pre-action notice to Defendant.
Defendant replied stating it would not pay severance allowance.
Claimants filed suit at National Industrial Court.

admitted_facts: Claimants served as councillors for two terms.
disputed_facts: Whether the cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011 or 2nd September 2014.
Whether the suit is statute barred.
background_facts: Claimants were elected councillors of Uzo-Uwani Local Government Area.
They sought payment of severance allowance for their second tenure.
facts.employment_relationship: Claimants were elected councillors, not employees under a contract of employment.
facts.contractual_relationship: Statutory relationship based on Local Government Law.

causes_of_action: Non-payment of severance allowance for second tenure as councillors.

claims.claim: Payment of N2.4 million each as severance allowance for second tenure, totaling N16.8 million for all claimants.
claims.legal_basis: Statutory entitlement under Local Government Law

claims.claim: Payment of N900,000 each as balance of severance allowance, totaling N6.3 million for all claimants.
claims.legal_basis: Statutory entitlement under Local Government Law

reliefs_sought.relief: An order for immediate release and payment of N2.4m each as severance allowance for second tenure, totaling N16.8M for all claimants.
An order for immediate release and payment of N900,000 each as balance of severance allowance, totaling N6.3m for all claimants.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether or not the suit is statute barred?
Whether or not the claimants can jointly file this suit as co-claimants?

questions_of_law: Whether the cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011 or 2nd September 2014.
Whether negotiations can extend the limitation period.

claimant_arguments: The cause of action accrued on 2nd September 2014 when the Defendant unequivocally stated it would not pay.
The Defendant is not entitled to protection of limitation law because it did not act in good faith.
The suit is not statute barred because time began to run from 2nd September 2014.
defendant_arguments: The suit is statute barred under section 136 of the Local Government Law Cap 109, Laws of Enugu State 2004, as it was filed more than six months after the cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011.
The claimants cannot jointly file this action as reliefs are personal to each claimant.
There is misjoinder of parties and causes of action.

party_authorities.proposition: Statute of limitation bars action not brought within six months.

party_authorities.authority: Fasein v. Oyerinde (1997) 11 NWLR (Pt. 530) at 553 SC
party_authorities.proposition: Defendant not entitled to protection of limitation law if not acting in good faith.

evidential_findings.finding: Cause of action arose on 31st December 2011, not 2nd September 2014.

findings_of_fact.issue: When did the cause of action accrue?
findings_of_fact.finding: The obligation to pay severance allowance arose on 31st December 2011.

findings_of_fact.issue: Was the suit filed within time?
findings_of_fact.finding: The suit was filed on 4th November 2014, more than six months after the cause of action accrued.

findings_of_law.issue: Whether the suit is statute barred
findings_of_law.finding: The suit is statute barred under section 136 of the Local Government Law Cap 109, Laws of Enugu State 2004.

findings_of_law.issue: Whether negotiations stop time from running
findings_of_law.finding: Negotiations between parties cannot stop the limitation time from running.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011 when the severance allowance became due. The suit was filed on 4th November 2014, beyond the six-month limitation period. The claimants' argument that time began to run from 2nd September 2014 is rejected because negotiations do not extend the limitation period. The allegation of bad faith is not supported by evidence.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether or not the suit is statute barred?

arguments.claimant: Cause of action accrued on 2nd September 2014; Defendant not entitled to limitation protection due to bad faith.
arguments.defendant: Suit statute barred under section 136 of Local Government Law; cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court examined the date of accrual of cause of action and found it to be 31st December 2011. The suit was filed on 4th November 2014, beyond the six-month period. Negotiations do not stop time from running. Bad faith not established.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A suit is statute barred if not filed within the time stipulated by law; negotiations do not extend the limitation period.
issue_analysis.result: Suit dismissed for being statute barred.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether or not the claimants can jointly file this suit as co-claimants?

arguments.claimant: Claimants can jointly file as co-claimants.
arguments.defendant: Reliefs are personal to each claimant; cannot be joint.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court did not make a specific finding on this issue as the suit was dismissed on the first issue.

ratio_decidendi.principle: A suit is statute barred if not filed within the time stipulated by law; negotiations do not extend the limitation period.
ratio_decidendi.application: The cause of action accrued on 31st December 2011; suit filed on 4th November 2014, beyond six months.

legal_principles.principle: Cause of action accrues when the injury or damage occurs.
legal_principles.context: Determining when time begins to run for limitation purposes.
legal_principles.source: Ezean v. Nigerian Railway Corporation (2015) 3 NWLR (Pt. 1445) 139 at 159.

legal_principles.principle: Negotiations between parties do not stop the limitation time from running.
legal_principles.context: Claimants argued that promises to pay extended the limitation period.

statutory_interpretation.statute: Local Government Law Cap 109, Laws of Enugu State 2004
statutory_interpretation.interpretation: Actions for failure to perform public duty must be commenced within six months.
statutory_interpretation.application: Claimants' action filed after six months from accrual of cause of action is statute barred.
